NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly assaulting police personnel and obstructing government work during a protest in the capital, news agency PTI reported, citing police sources on Thursday.The FIR invokes various sections related to allegedly assaulting and manhandling police personnel, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and misbehaviour with police officers.The action comes a day after INDIA bloc MPs were stopped by Delhi Police while attempting to march towards Jantar Mantar for a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Several other Congress leaders and party workers who took part in the demonstration have also been named in the FIR, police sources said.Police are examining the allegations and the role of those involved in the protest.Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul, Priyanka had led INDIA bloc leaders in a street protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Police detained 91 people during the demonstration, including several MPs and other political leaders.The protest took an intense turn after police stopped the protesters while they were travelling in buses towards Jantar Mantar for a surprise sit-in.The leaders had earlier attended a lunch meeting at a South Indian vegetarian restaurant on Janpath.Priyanka and several other women leaders lay on the road holding copies of the Constitution. NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday clarified his decision to skip Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's lunch meeting for INDIA bloc MPs, saying opposition leaders could meet over tea or even sit down for samosas in the future.Asked about his absence from the lunch, Yadav said, “It won’t just be about a single lunch. In the future, you might hear about a meeting over tea. We could all sit down and eat samosas too—if a ‘samosa’ slogan were to be raised, there’s nothing wrong with that. Diplomacy will continue”The SP chief had participated in the INDIA bloc's protest on the first day on Tuesday, when opposition MPs marched towards the Election Commission demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Yadav was among the leaders detained by Delhi Police during the protest.However, he did not join Rahul Gandhi and other Congress leaders in their subsequent sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan, where they remained for hours before being detained. Yadav later returned to Lucknow.On Wednesday, Yadav and other SP MPs also stayed away from Kharge's lunch at Sagar Ratna on Janpath and the protest march to Jantar Mantar that followed. The absence came amid questions over coordination between the SP and Congress, the two major constituents of the INDIA bloc, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.The lunch was organised as opposition MPs sought to chalk out their next steps in the campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and their allegations of “vote chori”. The MPs later boarded buses for Jantar Mantar, where they staged another protest demanding CEC's resignation.Rahul Gandhi, who was detained by police while heading towards Jantar Mantar, reiterated that the opposition would continue its protest until Kumar resigns. “We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us,” Gandhi said in a post on X.The developments followed Tuesday's dramatic protest, when opposition MPs were stopped near central Delhi while attempting to march to the Election Commission. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra later reached Akashvani Bhavan and staged an extended sit-in, while several other leaders, including Yadav, were detained during the day's demonstrations.

NEW DELHI: The President, world leaders and BJP-led NDA members Wednesday congratulated PM Narendra Modi on his 25-year unbroken stint as head of govt, with President Droupadi Murmu saying the momentous milestone reflected his steadfast commitment to people's well-being and India's progress."The transformation witnessed across our country in recent years is visible in the lives of people," she said.Home minister Amit Shah said Modi's journey of service, struggle and dedication since 2001 was synonymous with the welfare of the poor, women's empowerment and prosperity of every section of society. Recalling his meeting in New Delhi in 2019 as a private citizen, Tobgay said he told the PM he saw him as an elder brother and "an avatar of Vishnu"."In our part of the world, I explained, enlightened rulers have long been regarded as such," Tobgay said, adding Modi awakened in Indians a "powerful belief in themselves and in their country".Belgium's PM Bart De Wever, Dominican PM Roosevelt Skerrit and Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sent congratulatory messages and praised Modi's leadership.

Article Title: Supreme Court to study plea for recall of split verdict on EC appointment law
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.On Sept 23, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the CJI from the selection panel should go to a Constitution bench.Justice Datta declined the Centre's request for such a reference, while Justice Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench.It had said due to a difference of opinion, the matter would be placed before CJI Surya Kant on the administrative side for the constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication.On Wednesday, a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. "We will examine and take a call," the CJI said.Sankaranarayanan told the bench that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, but the matter had been released and he was asked to mention it before the CJI.When the CJI asked whether there was any other interlocutory application, Sankaranarayanan said a curative petition had also been filed. "That, I think, will have to go in its own form," he said.The petitions had challenged the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which replaced the selection mechanism laid down by SC in its March 2, 2023 judgement.In that ruling, a five-judge Constitution bench had directed that the CEC and ECs be appointed by the President on the advice of a committee comprising the PM, the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha and the CJI. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 law, under which the selection committee comprises the PM, a Un-ion Cabinet minister nominated by the PM and the leader of the opposition in LS.
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict. Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the CJI should go to a Constitution bench.

Article Title: A quick lunch, then a Jantar Mantar march: How Rahul-led opposition once again kept police guessing

NEW DELHI: On Wednesday afternoon, Congress and INDIA bloc leaders were meeting for lunch at a restaurant on Janpath. Within an hour, they were boarding buses and heading towards Jantar Mantar for a protest.The demonstration quickly took a different turn when Delhi Police stopped the buses on Ashoka Road, setting off another confrontation between Congress leaders and the police.The episode was the latest example of a 'dhappa' style protest that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have recently used.The latest episode began after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge announced an INDIA bloc sit-in at Jantar Mantar following the lunch."Today, we will hold a sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar. Until our demands are met, we will continue to stage such protests," Kharge announced.Delhi Police stopped the buses carrying the MPs and officers, citing a Supreme Court directive, said permission for protests at Jantar Mantar had to be sought at least 10 days in advance.The confrontation soon escalated. Congress MPs climbed on top of a bus, while Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said, "This is Rahul Gandhi's 'sena,' we won't stop."Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other women MPs lay down on the road, while Congress workers punctured the tyres of the bus carrying Rahul Gandhi.Priyanka alleged that she was manhandled, while TMC MP Mahua Moitra alleged a lathi-charge. Police eventually detained the MPs following a brief struggle.The events followed a similar sequence a day earlier, when Rahul announced that INDIA bloc MPs would march from Parliament House to the Election Commission headquarters to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.This time, too, police were prepared. Barricades, paramilitary personnel and traffic diversions were put in place. Rahul climbed a barricade and waved the national flag before the march was stopped and several leaders were detained.But the protest did not end there.As MPs were being put into buses, Priyanka boarded one and Rahul appeared ready to follow. The two then changed course and entered the nearby Akashvani Bhawan premises.They sat under a tree near Gate No. 4, where broadcasting staff gathered outside to watch. KC Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi and Srinivas BV joined them, while other Congress workers climbed the boundary wall and raised slogans.Congress later circulated a video of the detour with a "dhappa" caption. After nearly nine hours, police forcibly removed Rahul, Priyanka and the other protesters.Delhi Police registered an FIR over their "unauthorised" entry into the premises. Rahul subsequently used the case as part of his political messaging."I have 45 FIRs against me. My goal is to have 100. I want 100 FIRs to be registered against me. Every FIR is a medal for me," he told reporters on Wednesday.The same approach had surfaced earlier on July 21, a day after police action against students and young people protesting at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak.Congress MPs had initially been asked to assemble at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10 Rajaji Marg to wish him on his birthday. Most MPs were not told about the larger plan in advance so that police could not prepare for the protest.After both Houses of Parliament were adjourned, Rahul and Priyanka walked towards the gate of 7 Lok Kalyan Marg, the Prime Minister's residence, around 500 metres away. Kharge and other MPs followed them.The leaders tied plastic bands around their hands and demanded the resignations of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged treatment of students during the march to Parliament.The government sent minister of state in the PMO Jitendra Singh and Union home secretary Govind Mohan to the spot. Jitendra Singh tried to convince Rahul to call off the protest, saying the area was not designated for demonstrations and that "It was causing significant inconvenience to the public."Rahul, Priyanka and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav were eventually removed by police and taken to Mandir Marg and Chhatrasal Stadium before being released.For Congress, the approach has also produced a dramatic visual narrative.The recent protests are centred on the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation after a report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken without their knowledge.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion of a breakdown in functioning, saying disagreements are normal in a multi-member body and that decisions were taken unanimously. The matter is before the Supreme Court.BJP chief Nitin Nabin, meanwhile, accused Rahul of working with anti-social elements and spreading anarchy.
Article Summary: The episode was the latest example of a 'dhappa' style protest that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have recently used. Congress MPs climbed on top of a bus, while Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said, "This is Rahul Gandhi's'sena,' we won't stop"

NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Wednesday made a startling allegation that Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar had conducted a sting operation against Siddaramaiah, forcing the veteran Congress leader to step down from the chief minister’s post.Kumaraswamy’s remarks came after Shivakumar reportedly told ministers at a cabinet meeting that a sting operation was being carried out against them."Due to the sting operation conducted by DK Shivakumar, the Congress high command insulted and removed Siddaramaiah from the CM post in a very humiliating manner. A news channel and the Congress high command joined hands with DK Shivakumar and removed Siddaramaiah. Siddaramaiah, who went to Delhi believing he was called to discuss cabinet expansion, was informed about the sting operation and his resignation was taken," the JDS leader alleged."The way his resignation was taken was not right. Congress did not treat such a senior leader properly. Who did all this? Who is behind it? Which media house is involved? Everyone knows," he asked.Kumaraswamy further claimed that some of his "friends" from the Congress itself told him that Shivakumar became CM through a sting operation.He described the chief minister as a "master at doing sting operation.""He is a master at doing sting operations. He is trying to keep all ministers under his control by conducting sting operations. He himself did the sting and is now trying to put the blame on opposition parties. If I have done any sting, let him take action. He has an SIT; he has even given it a Rs 35 lakh award! Let him get it investigated. Who has stopped him?" the Union minister stated."In the past, development issues were discussed in cabinet meetings. Now in DK Shivakumar's time, honeytrap, sting operations are being discussed. Instead, from morning till evening he sits doing sting operations. His own party MLAs come and tell me. This is the sorry state of affairs this state has come to," he added.Shivakumar became Karnataka chief minister in June, after his party colleague and political rival Siddaramaiah resigned nearly three years into his second stint as chief minister, which began in May 2023. Shivakumar served as deputy chief minister under a reported power-sharing arrangement, under which Siddaramaiah was expected to step down after completing 2.5 years of his second term.

Article Title: Rupi Soren, mother of Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren, dies in Ranchi

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren ’s mother, Rupi Soren, passed away at a hospital in Ranchi, an official told news agency PTI."CM Hemant Soren's mother Rupi Soren, who was admitted here, passed away around 8.30 pm. She was admitted to the hospital on September 18 with breathing difficulty," Director of Hill View Hospital and Research Centre, Dr Nitesh Priya, told PTI.She was a key figure in the Soren family and had been caring for her ailing husband, veteran JMM leader Shibu Soren, who is fondly known as “Guruji”.Rupi had also been involved in politics herself. She contested the Dumka Lok Sabha election in 1999 in undivided Bihar but lost to Babulal Marandi by fewer than 5,000 votes.Hemant Soren, who visited his mother earlier on Wednesday, paid an emotional tribute on social media: “After Baba left, Maa was my greatest shelter. May God grant strength to the bereaved family to bear this immense sorrow. Om Shanti!”Champai Soren said, “The sad news of the passing of Smt Rupi Soren ji, wife of the late Shibu Soren ji has left my heart in pain. Many events and memories from the time of the Jharkhand movement are flashing before my eyes. May Marang Buru (the supreme tribal deity) grant peace to the departed soul and give strength to the family.”
Article Summary: Rupi Soren was a key figure in the Soren family. She had been caring for her ailing husband, veteran JMM leader Shibu Soren. She contested the Dumka Lok Sabha election in 1999 in undivided Bihar.

(sic)Tharoor, however, appeared unwilling to take the bait said,It wouldn’t, if I had the slightest idea what you are referring to! Do enlighten me." (sic)Das then spelt out the reference, invoking the metaphor that Tharoor had quoted in 2018.“Dr. Tharoor, I speak, of course, of that immortal zoological-theological conundrum involving a scorpion and the impracticability of a chappal. In the context of the video, surely it warrants a reprise” (sic)The exchange referred to Tharoor’s 2018 remarks in Bengaluru, when he quoted an unnamed RSS source who had allegedly described PM Modi as “a scorpion sitting on a Shivling”.Speaking at the event in 2018, Tharoor had said, “There's an extraordinarily striking metaphor expressed by an unnamed RSS source to journalist Vinod Jose, that, 'Modi is like a scorpion sitting on a Shivling, you can't remove him with your hand and you cannot hit it with a chappal either' ...because while removing him with a hand would mean you'd end up getting stung, hitting the Shivaling with a chappal would raise questions on the spiritual tenets you have been practicing for years. ”Also read: RSS source said Modi is like a 'scorpion sitting on a Shivling': Tharoor The latest exchange unfolded against the backdrop of a political confrontation in Delhi over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Jantar Mantar turned into a political battleground on Wednesday as Opposition leaders seeking to march towards the protest site were stopped by Delhi Police.Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were among those detained, while opposition leaders vowed to intensify their campaign seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The standoff unfolded amid heavy security near the designated protest site. Rahul Gandhi attempted to open a barricaded gate as Opposition MPs sought to proceed towards Jantar Mantar, but police pushed the protesters back and detained several leaders.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was later seen lying on the ground and alleged that women police personnel had scratched her and thrown protesters to the ground. Rahul Gandhi, while being detained, was seen waving at the media and showing a victory sign.As the confrontation over SIR intensified, the CJP announced a fresh youth-led protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10.CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had formally intimated Delhi Police about the proposed demonstration, with young people from across the country expected to gather over what the party described as “theft of votes”, “hijacking of elections” and the alleged exclusion of Gen Z from voter lists.For now, however, Das’s attempt to revive Tharoor’s most famous zoological metaphor has produced no fresh verdict from the Congress leader.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor sidestepped an attempt by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das to draw him into commenting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The exchange began after PM Modi visited the Shri Vinayak Mandir in New Delhi on Wednesday, the day he completed 25 uninterrupted years.

Article Title: 'FIRs are like medals, I want 100': Rahul Gandhi ups ante against Gyanesh Kumar, seeks resignation
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi stepped up his attack on Gyanesh Kumar who has faced opposition criticism over his functioning.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Gyanesh Kumar resign as Chief Election Commissioner? Yes, he has lost legitimacy. No, he is doing his job. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday struck a defiant note over the 45 FIRs against him, saying every such FIR is a "medal" for him and that his "goal is to have 100 FIRs".The Congress leader also stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who has been in the opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent among his subordinates.Rahul Gandhi, while declaring an impromptu protest from Jantar Mantar, said, "Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief."Our plan is to go to the designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, and sit there together once again, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate Election Commissioner of the country," he said.The Raebareli Lok Sabha MP attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, alleging that the trio, in cahoots with Gyanesh Kumar have "destroyed the democracy of the country"."Modi Ji, Amit Shah Ji, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar have destroyed the democracy of the country. As I said yesterday, those who have done this are traitors to the country, and we will take action against them.I am telling you right now: Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," the Congress scion claimed.When asked about the FIR against him, he says, "I have 45 FIRs against me. My goal is to have 100. I want 100 FIRs to be registered against me. Every FIR is a medal for me."The opposition has upped the ante against Gyanesh Kumar. On Tuesday, the parties staged a day long protest which culminated in the Rahul Gandhi's detention. The opposition parties are also holding parallel protests across states, with the Congress signalling that the face-off will continue till the CEC resigns.Meanwhile, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders and workers were stopped by police personnel at barricades on Wednesday as they staged a protest march from the Sindhi Academy near Kashmere Gate towards the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office, alleging widespread "vote theft."
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi says every FIR is a "medal" for him and that his "goal is to have 100 FIRs" The Congress leader also stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar has been in the opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: India bloc protest: Rahul 'inappropriately touched' woman cop, Priyanka 'punched' another, alleges BJP
Article Text:
Leaders from the BJP have accused Rahul Gandhi of inappropriately touching a police constable and Priyanka Gandhi of physically assaulting an officer

BJP alleges Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi attacked cops

BJP invokes Congress slogans over alleged police misconduct

BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over FIR remark

BJP alleges ‘Nepal- and Bangladesh-like anarchy’

BJP says protests will not affect Supreme Court case

BJP alleges ‘global international forces’ backing Rahul

Rahul, INDIA bloc leaders detained during protests





NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday accused Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra of misbehaving with police personnel during recent anti-CEC protests in the national capital, alleging that Rahul Gandhi "inappropriately touched" a woman constable and Priyanka "punched" a female police officer.The BJP also accused the Congress of trying to create "Nepal- and Bangladesh-like anarchy" through its street protests.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, spokesperson Sidharth Yadav alleged that Rahul and Priyanka were spreading "anarchy" in Delhi and had attacked police personnel during the protests.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari separately alleged that Rahul Gandhi was "desperate" to come to power and accused the Congress of seeking to create unrest in the country.Yadav said the visuals being circulated were not of a protest but showed "the anarchy being spread in the national capital" under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress."There is no ordinary citizen, no member of the general public, participating in these protests," he alleged.Yadav alleged that Rahul "inappropriately touched" a woman police constable and claimed that Priyanka "punched a female police officer in the stomach"."The conduct of Rahul Gandhi in inappropriately touching a female constable is totally unacceptable," he said."Priyanka who punched a female police officer in the stomach even though she was simply standing there and had not provoked anyone. This is beyond tolerance," he said.The BJP spokesperson also alleged that Congress workers kicked policemen after bringing them to the ground."Is this what the Congress's 'Mohabbat ki Dukan' is? The hateful merchandise being sold in this 'Mohabbat ki Dukan' is now out in the open before the country," Yadav said.Referring to Rahul Gandhi's slogan "smash the patriarchy" and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's "Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon" slogans, Yadav questioned whether the alleged conduct of the Congress leaders was consistent with their stated positions."When she was hitting that female police officer, was this the slogan that was going through her mind?" he asked, referring to Priyanka.Yadav said if that was not the case, "then the truth behind their slogans is now before the country"."Rahul Gandhi has said that there are 47 FIRs against him. But wearing an FIR relating to an alleged crime against a woman as a medal - only Rahul Gandhi can do this in the country," he said.BJP spokesperson Bhandari showed some video footage purportedly of the INDIA bloc's protest on Wednesday and said the manner in which Rahul, his sister Priyanka and Congress workers allegedly manhandled police personnel in Delhi made the party's "intention" clear."The Congress party's strategy is to spread anarchy in India, like Nepal and Bangladesh," he said in a video message.Overlaying a purported video of the Congress protest in his video message, Bhandari said, "Congress party workers are seen trying to assault police personnel with kicks and punches. The policeman is performing his duty there, but a Congress worker pushes him and then kicks him."Showing another such video, he claimed police personnel were requesting Rahul Gandhi to hold a peaceful protest as "there is a crowd of thousands" accompanying him.He also alleged that Rahul pushed a policeman hoping to create "resistance reels"."In the third clip, Priyanka Vadra herself is seen attempting to push police personnel," Bhandari said.On the Election Commission issue, Bhandari said the matter was already before the Supreme Court and claimed that the protests would have no bearing on the judicial proceedings."When the matter is before the Supreme Court, whether I protest on the streets, someone else does, or Rahul Gandhi does, it will not make any difference to the court," he said."Rahul Gandhi thinks that through such visuals, he can put pressure on the Supreme Court's decision and interfere in the judicial process," he said.He also alleged that "global international forces" were working along with Rahul Gandhi to create unrest in India."India's democracy is alive, strong and secure, and there is peace in the country. Are some global international forces, along with Rahul Gandhi, who is desperate to come to power, trying to bring the family back to power by burning the country and creating anarchy in it?" he said."The country is watching. Rahul Gandhi's intention is not democracy, but the family; not the country, instead it is to support the forces that are trying to burn the country," Bhandari said.Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders held street protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Tuesday and Wednesday. They were detained on both days and later released.On Thursday too, INDIA bloc leaders were meeting for lunch at a restaurant, and sources said another protest could take place afterwards.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: BJP accuses Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra of misbehaving with police personnel during recent anti-CEC protests. The BJP also accused the Congress of trying to create "Nepal- and Bangladesh-like anarchy" through its street protests.

Article Title: FIR against independent candidate for procession sans nod
Article Text:
The FIR has been registered at Begumpura police station

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The city police have registered an FIR against independent candidate Ramesh Kasare Patil and 12 others for allegedly violating prohibitory orders by taking out a symbolic funeral procession on Tuesday afternoon.The FIR was registered at Begumpura police station under section 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act on the complaint of police constable Pandurang Gore.Patil allegedly joined a symbolic funeral procession at Chandane Chowk after filing his nomination for Aurangabad Graduate Constituency election around 11.30am on Tuesday. Inspector Pravina Yadav said Patil lay on a symbolic bier while an unlawful assembly held the procession near the MLC nomination venue.According to the FIR, Patil’s supporters also played drums and raised slogans during the procession. Police said no permission was granted to the candidate or his supporters to hold any agitation, procession or demonstration while filing the nomination. The procession allegedly violated the prohibitory order issued by police commissioner Pravin Pawar on Sept 30.The incident took place around 12.40pm on the road between Chandane Chowk and Annabhau Sathe Chowk, while the case was registered late on Tuesday. The other accused named in the FIR are Vilas Sonawane, Mahadev Amle, Bhagwat Kale, Ranganath Chapate, Santosh Jadhav, Nita Kale, Shivaji Sadge, Sitaram Naik, Sopan Kale, Sharad Galbe and Arun alias Chhotu Shrisundar.
Article Summary: Independent candidate Ramesh Kasare Patil and 12 others allegedly violated prohibitory orders by taking out a symbolic funeral procession on Tuesday afternoon. The procession allegedly violated the prohibitory order issued by police commissioner Pravin Pawar on Sept 30. The incident took place on the road between Chandane Chowk and Annabhau Sathe Chowk.

Article Title: 'Fadnavis, why are you trying to become Yogi Adityanath': Abhijeet Dipke questions Chandrapur cops’ notices to Delhi-bound members
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke addresses a press conference, in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday questioned the Chandrapur police for issuing notices to CJP supporters to prevent them from travelling to participate in a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.He also criticised chief minister Devendra Fadnavis over the issue. “Fadnavis, why are you trying to become Yogi Adityanath? This is Maharashtra,” he said.Dipke said that the notice sought details about the source of funds for the agitation and warned against posting protest-related content on social media, citing possibility of violence.“How does Chandrapur police know the protest will turn violent? Does Jantar Mantar fall in Chandrapur?” he asked reporters in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.He claimed that such notices were tarnishing the image of Maharashtra Police. “They should not act like Delhi Police,” he said.Dipke said volunteers in Maharashtra and Rajasthan were served notices. “Instead of harassing my colleagues, arrest me... Apply whatever laws you want against me, but do not trouble my colleagues,” he said, reiterating the outfit’s demand for resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the Chandrapur police for issuing notices to CJP supporters to prevent them from travelling to participate in a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Dipke said that the notice sought details about the source of funds for the agitation and warned against posting protest-related content on social media.

Article Title: Kolhapur tutor kidnapped from Latur home, murdered in Beed over suspicion of affair, four arrested
Article Text:
File photo :

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 32-year-old tutor was allegedly called out of his home in Latur, abducted and taken to a stone-crushing centre in neighbouring Beed district, where four men beat him to death on suspicion that he was having an affair with a woman, police said.One of the accused later took the unconscious victim, Madhav alias Nitin Dhanaji Sangme, to Govt Medical College and Hospital in Latur. He allegedly told doctors that Sangme had been found injured near Bardapur. Doctors declared Sangme dead.Police at the hospital became suspicious of the account. They questioned the accused, and the alleged abduction and assault came to light.Sangme worked as a tutor with a private coaching class in Kolhapur. He had returned to his home in Latur for preparations for his brother’s engagement.Police said Sangme was called to Vitthal-Rukmini temple area near Kanheri Chowk on Sunday afternoon. Four men allegedly bundled him into a car and drove him to a stone-crushing centre at Bardapur in Beed district’s Ambajogai taluka.Latur SP Amol Tambe said the accused suspected Sangme of having an affair with a woman.“The victim was assaulted with iron rods, belts and sticks. The investigation is underway to establish the exact circumstances leading to the murder ,” Tambe said.Police identified the accused as Prithviraj Deshmukh, Dhawal Deshmukh, Prathamesh Reddy and Aditya Bhalke, all residents of Latur.The four allegedly assaulted Sangme until he lost consciousness. Bhalke then took him to the Latur hospital and claimed that he had found Sangme injured near Bardapur, police said.Shivajinagar police personnel at the hospital questioned Bhalke after becoming suspicious of his version. The alleged abduction and assault emerged during questioning.Inspector Santosh Patil, who is investigating the case, said police were verifying the sequence of events and the role of each accused. “We have registered a case of abduction and murder and are investigating the motive,” Patil said.Shivajinagar police registered the case on a complaint lodged by Sangme’s younger brother Narendra.The four accused were produced before a court on Tuesday and remanded in police custody for four days. Police are now collecting evidence linked to the murder.
Article Summary: Madhav alias Nitin Dhanaji Sangme, 32, was abducted from his home in Latur. Four men allegedly bundled him into a car and drove him to a stone-crushing centre at Bardapur in Beed district’s Ambajogai taluka. The four allegedly assaulted Sangme until he lost consciousness.

Article Title: Gokul poll: NCP gets 9 seats, BJP & Sena 7 each, and JSSP 2
Article Text:
Mahayuti politicians discuss seat sharing for Gokul election

Kolhapur

:





After several rounds of closed-door negotiations and bickering, Mahayuti functionaries in Kolhapur on Wednesday finalised a seat-sharing pact for the Oct 18 election to the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul.The cooperative dairy, which has an annual turnover of around Rs 3,000 crore, elects 25 directors every five years.Announcing the formula after a meeting on Wednesday evening, BJP minister Chandrakant Patil said, “NCP is going to contest on nine seats, and BJP and Shiv Sena on seven seats each. Jansurajya Shakti Party has two seats. Minister Hasan Mushrif will announce the list of our 25 candidates on Thursday on social media,” Patil said. NCP is expected to accommodate the front led by Shirol MLA Rajendra Patil Yadravkar from its quota.Having settled the arithmetic, Mahayuti now faces a tougher challenge: convincing a large number of ticket aspirants to withdraw. Several supporters have filed nominations hoping to find a place on the alliance panel.Mushrif acknowledged the difficult task ahead before heading into the nearly three-hour meeting with Mahayuti politicians at a Kolhapur hotel.“I have experienced a night before finalising candidates for last five decades. One should take the tough call, try to convince the supporters to withdraw,” he said.Meanwhile, Congress MLC Satej Patil, who was expected to announce his panel against Mahayuti on Wednesday, deferred the announcement to Thursday afternoon. Sources said he could seek to tap discontent among Mahayuti aspirants left out of the final panel to strengthen his challenge.
Article Summary: Mahayuti functionaries in Kolhapur on Wednesday finalised a seat-sharing pact for the Oct 18 election. NCP is expected to accommodate the front led by Shirol MLA Rajendra Patil Yadravkar from its quota. Mahayuti now faces a tougher challenge: convincing a large number of ticket aspirants to withdraw.

Article Title: Mahayuti to fight Gokul dairy election collectively, Fadnavis leaves lead role to Mushrif
Article Text:
Kolhapur

Gokul Election In A Nutshell





: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has said there will be no intervention at his level in the election for Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy, and NCP leader and minister Hasan Mushrif is taking the lead on behalf of Mahayuti.Fadnavis’s remarks have come amid talks to hold the election unopposed, ceding some seats to the panel led by Congress MLC Satej Patil to avoid an election amid the ongoing drought crisis. “Mahayuti partners will contest Gokul election in alliance. At present, Gokul dairy is led by Hasan Mushrif and he is also taking lead for the election. The leaders of Mahayuti’s partners be it Chandrakant Patil, Mahadik’s, Prakash Abitkar, Rajesh Kshirsagar and their supporters will work together. Gokul dairy’s election is local and limited to cooperative sector. Therefore, at my level, there will be no intervention,” said Fadnavis.Thursday, Oct 8, is the last day for the withdrawal of the nomination, while the final list of the candidates will be released and the distribution of the symbols carried out on Friday. There are 25 posts of directors for Gokul dairy election. The dairy, which supplies milk to Mumbai, Pune and Goa, has a total turnover of around Rs 3,000 crore and is connected to most of the rural households in Kolhapur district, and is therefore politically sensitive.The seat-sharing within Mahayuti has been stuck. Mushrif wants a larger share for his party, while BJP wants no less than what Mushrif will get.Meanwhile, Satej Patil, Congress MLC, has declared that come what may, there will be no unopposed election for Gokul. “Rumours are being spread about making the election uncontested; this is being done by BJP to corner Mushrif. I am clear on this: we have 25 candidates who have filed nominations, and I am going to announce our panel on Wednesday. If the Mahayuti wants to make the Gokul election unopposed, citing drought conditions, why is it not proposing the same for other ongoing cooperative elections, such as Sangli and Satara district central cooperative banks?” said Patil.Total directors to be elected: 25Total Primary Dairies Eligible To Depute A Delegate To Cast A Vote: 5,423Total Nominations: 240Voting: Oct 18Counting of votes and day of result: Oct 19
Article Summary: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has said there will be no intervention at his level in the election for Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy. NCP leader and minister Hasan Mushrif is taking the lead on behalf of Mahayuti. The dairy supplies milk to Mumbai, Pune and Goa.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Can suppression of purchase of property vitiate one’s election? asks HC
Article Text:
High court Madras High Court

Chennai:





Can suppression of the purchase of a property worth a few lakhs, by a person who owns properties worth more than ₹600 crore, amount to undue influence of a voter? If one goes to a house of a voter and gives him ₹500 to vote for him, it would constitute undue influence, not mere suppression of purchase of a property, Madras high court said on Wednesday while hearing a plea challenging the election of minister C Joseph Vijay from Perambur assembly constituency.When Vijay, a super star in cinema, has disclosed more than ₹600 crore, will non-disclosure of a few lakhs vitiate his election, Justice V Lakshminarayanan wondered.Responding, N C Ashok Kumar, counsel for petitioner Dinesh , a voter from Perambur, said that tendering money cannot simply be equated with the entire definition of undue influence under the Representation of People Act. This apart, the court should not decide the substantiality, truth or ultimate tenability of the allegation at this stage of deciding an application seeking to reject the plaint, provided the petition contains the necessary material facts and particulars, he said. “If an act is calculated to interfere with the free exercise of an electoral right, that is the true and effective test of whether or not a candidate is guilty of undue influence,” counsel added.Secondly, contesting an election is not a fundamental right. It is governed by a statute. When a statute requires a particular thing to be done in a particular manner, it must be followed, Ashok Kumar said. “Nobody compels a person to contest an election. But once a person chooses to contest, he has to comply with the statutory requirements,” he added.Recording the submissions, the court adjourned the hearing to Thursday.
Article Summary: If one goes to a house of a voter and gives him ₹500 to vote for him, it would constitute undue influence, Madras high court said on Wednesday while hearing a plea challenging the election of minister C Joseph Vijay from Perambur assembly constituency.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: EVMs, VVPATs secured under two-tier armed cover, 24x7 CCTV surveillance
Article Text:
Representative image





TIRUPUR: Electronic voting machines (EVMs) and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) units used for the Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district have been placed in a strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance, officials said.After the completion of polling on Oct 6, the EVMs and VVPAT units were brought to the counting centre located at LRG Govt Women’s Arts College in the district.District election officer and collector Dr Manish Narnaware and election general observer Chinmay Pundlikrao Gotmare, IAS, on Wednesday supervised the placement of machines into the strong room in the presence of candidates and their agents. The strong room was sealed thereafter, with the participation of superintendent of police Srishti Singh, IPS, deputy commissioner of police Akash Joshi, IPS, and Dharapuram revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja.Narnaware said the strong room would be opened on Oct 9 -- the counting day -- in the presence of candidates or their representatives and the central observer, under videography.District election authorities said the strong room was being protected with armed security personnel in a two-tier arrangement, with continuous monitoring through CCTV cameras.To ensure uninterrupted supervision of CCTV feeds, three officers of deputy collector rank have been deployed daily at the district level, while separate monitoring officers have been appointed for the assembly constituency.The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.Authorities said all contesting candidates have been informed in writing about appointing representatives to observe the security arrangements, with permission granted for such representatives to stay outside the inner security cordon.Polling was held at 320 booths in the constituency. There are 2,23,306 registered voters, and 1,79,214 votes were cast, recording a turnout of 80.25%.
Article Summary: Electronic voting machines used for Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district. EVMs and VVPAT units placed in strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.

Article Title: FIR against Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving child in poll campaign in Dharapuram
Article Text:
Authorities in Dharapuram have filed a case against Udhayanidhi Stalin for infringing on the Model Code of Conduct during a recent election rally





TIRUPUR: Dharapuram Police have registered a case against Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram, where the Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll.According to a press release issued by Tirupur district police, the incident took place on Saturday near the Periyar statue in Dharapuram town during an election campaign meeting addressed by Udhayanidhi.Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in any election-related activities.Police said Udhayanidhi made a child speak at the campaign meeting in a manner that was insulting to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and also used the child for election campaigning.Dharapuram Town Police registered a case against Udhayanidhi. Further investigation is under way, police said.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin involved a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram. The Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll. Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in election-related activities.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Satheesan joins Delhi protest, hits out at Centre & EC
Article Text:
V D Satheesan at the protest site in New Delhi on Wednesday

New Delhi/T’puram:





CM V D Satheesan joined the escalating demonstrations by the opposition parties in New Delhi, voicing support for leader of the opposition in LS Rahul Gandhi while accusing Centre and Election Commission (EC) of systematically compromising the democratic process. Satheesan condemned the police action against opposition leaders, accusing the cops of using brutal force and denying the basic right to protest at a venue like Jantar Mantar.Satheesan reached the police station where Rahul was being held but was initially denied permission to meet him. He told the police that he too should be arrested if he was not allowed to meet Rahul. He was subsequently allowed to enter and meet him.“I met and spoke with him. He has inspired democratic-minded people like me in this country. We will stand behind him. This is a fight to protect democracy,” said Satheesan. He pledged that Keralam stands firmly behind the protest, which he predicted will intensify across the country in the coming weeks.The standoff follows days of high-voltage demonstrations led by Rahul and INDI alliance at Jantar Mantar and Parliament Street.Opposition leaders are demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll manipulations, referred to by protesters as ‘vote chori’, during the special intensive revision process.“In our democratic country, EC has sabotaged the voters’ list. This is part of a conspiracy between Centre and EC. Millions of legitimate voters were deliberately purged from the voters’ lists to influence election outcomes in favour of the ruling party. The truth has now come out and it is that BJP managed to win elections in various parts by sabotaging the election process. Rahul is fighting against this manipulation. I’m participating in the protest proudly as this protest will be marked in golden letters in the country’s history,” he said.Questioning the police action against Rahul, Satheesan asked whether India had become a dictatorship if the leader of the opposition in LS was not allowed to stage a protest at Jantar Mantar. “If the leader of the opposition of India is told that he has no right to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar, is this a dictatorial country?” he asked.Despite heavy police barricading, high-profile detentions (including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi ) and new FIRs, the opposition remains resolute, he said. Satheesan reaffirmed that the agitation is far from over and framed it as a critical fight to safeguard constitutional principles and restore faith in the country’s voting system.
Article Summary: Satheesan condemned the police action against opposition leaders, accusing the cops of using brutal force and denying the basic right to protest. Satheesan reaffirmed that the agitation is far from over and framed it as a critical fight to safeguard constitutional principles and restore faith in the country’s voting system.

Article Title: Firm, three others booked over alleged overseas job fraud
Article Text:
Kochi:





Ernakulam Central Police have registered two separate cases against a private firm and three persons for allegedly cheating two men from Munambam of Rs 4.3 lakh by promising them jobs in Netherlands and Luxembourg.The cases were registered on Wednesday based on complaints alleging that the accused collected money through Snehayathra Associates Pvt Ltd on Market Road, Ernakulam.According to the police, one complainant alleged that Rs 2.3 lakh was collected from him in three instalments between June 4 and Aug 5, 2025.In the second case, the complainant alleged that Rs 2 lakh was collected from him in three instalments between Oct 16, 2024, and Aug 5, 2025, on the promise of securing a job abroad.Both complainants alleged that the job was not arranged, and the money was not returned.The police named Sheeba Raphel, Raakz Agencies and Sahila Shamsudheen as accused in both cases. The FIR in the case has invoked Sections 318(4) (cheating) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.According to the police, further investigation is under way to ascertain the full details of the alleged fraud and the role of the accused.Kaapa invoked against repeat offender: A 28-year-old man from Kothamangalam was detained under Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (Kaapa).The accused, Ebin Tomy of Chirappadi, Iramalloor, was lodged at Viyyur Central Jail following a report submitted by Ernakulam Rural district police chief K S Sudarshan. The detention order was issued by district collector Priyanka G on Wednesday.Tomy is involved in several cases registered at Kothamangalam, Perumbavoor, Vazhakulam, Kodanad, Alappuzha North and Poovar police stations. The cases include attempt to murder, robbery, kidnapping, theft and offences against women.According to the police, the latest case was registered in Perumbavoor in July after he allegedly entered an unoccupied house with the intention of committing theft and attempted to sexually assault a woman who arrived at the house.
Article Summary: Cases were registered on Wednesday based on complaints alleging that the accused collected money through Snehayathra Associates Pvt Ltd. Police named Sheeba Raphel, Raakz Agencies and Sahila Shamsudheen as accused in both cases.
